name: Paracetamol
summary: Paracetamol (acetaminophen) is an analgesic and antipyretic used to treat fever and mild to moderate pain. Excessive amounts can cause severe liver injury.
metabolism: Well absorbed by mouth and by rectum. Given rectally it reaches a peak blood level after 2 to 3 hours and stays in the body for about 2 hours. It is broken down mostly in the liver, where glucuronic acid and sulphate are joined onto it. A small amount, about 3-10% of a therapeutic dose, goes through oxidation instead, and the reactive breakdown product that forms is grabbed by glutathione in the liver and leaves as cystein and mercapturic acid conjugates. It leaves through the kidneys: 2-3% of a therapeutic dose comes out unchanged, 80-90% as the glucuronide and sulphate, and a smaller amount as the cystein and mercapturic acid derivatives.
